items.claim: The one-verse cut at the vindication oracle stands: a verse-initial divine messenger frame opens it, both edges are byte-distinct from their neighbours, and the two holiness objects inside the verse are correctly kept apart.
items.evidence: Re-collated at byte tier against oshb:Isa.49.7: the verse opens כֹּ֣ה אָֽמַר יְהוָה֩ - a divine-owned frame, not one of the four narrative-zone verses where a named human king or his envoy carries the same formula. The two holiness objects are byte-distinct inside this one verse: the suffixed epithet קְדוֹשׁ֗וֹ early, and the signature title construct in its DEFECTIVE spelling קְדֹ֥שׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל at the close - a plene-only needle would miss this title site altogether, and the row quotes the attested defective form rather than a normalised one (title-construct sweep: 25 verses book-wide, verse counts; the trisagion is a separate object and is not invoked here). The front-seam contrast holds on the bytes: oshb:Isa.49.5 carries its divine-speech signature embedded as וְעַתָּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה inside a first-person report, and oshb:Isa.49.6 opens with a bare וַיֹּ֗אמֶר - neither is a verse-initial messenger frame, so the contrast drawn against the preceding report is byte-true and not merely an English impression. The back seam is a frame-to-frame join: oshb:Isa.49.8 opens כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה, byte-confirmed and separately worded. The setumah cited at oshb:Isa.49.6 is in the mark inventory under that exact type (single witness), no petuchah or setumah falls inside the span, so span-relevant symmetry is complete; the servant-referent material is disclosed without being decided, as required. Residue only, not a defect: oshb:Isa.49.6 is also a ketiv/qere-bearing verse and the row does not say so, but it neither counts nor slices there.

items.claim: The five-verse promise unit holds: its opening frame and its closing verse are byte-confirmed, and the one interior device that could rival them is subordinate on the bytes.
items.evidence: The opening formula re-collates at byte tier as כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.49.8), verse-initial and divine, separately worded from the frame one verse back. The interior carries a rival the row never names: oshb:Isa.49.9 opens לֵאמֹ֤ר לַֽאֲסוּרִים֙ צֵ֔אוּ - an infinitive of speech governing imperatives addressed to the bound. Byte-checked, that infinitive is subordinate to the frame already opened and carries no independent frame token, so it does not defeat the cut; the row's denial of an imperative at the next turn is likewise byte-true, since oshb:Isa.49.10 opens לֹ֤א יִרְעָ֨בוּ֙ in the third person. The closing verse re-collates at byte tier and opens with a presentative rather than a frame, so nothing competes at the back edge before the imperative onset one verse later. No petuchah or setumah falls anywhere in oshb:Isa.49.8-Isa.49.12, so span-relevant mark symmetry is satisfied by the row's silence and absence is not counterevidence; a paseq is inventoried at oshb:Isa.49.8 but is count-only and unpositionable, so nothing is owed there either. All refs sit in identity-numbered chapters, so no crosswalk qualifier is at issue anywhere in this span.

items.claim: The one-verse doxology cut is byte-supported at both edges, and its ketiv/qere apparatus is disclosed with both staged forms present rather than silently resolved.
items.evidence: oshb:Isa.49.13 opens רָנּ֤וּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ at byte tier - a plural imperative with a cosmic vocative, followed by a second addressee and a third imperative; both witnesses render all three as commands (web:Isa.49.13), so the form-class label stands even though no morphology layer is staged. The ketiv/qere disclosure is correct against the inventory: this verse is one of the ketiv/qere-bearing verses, and the row's quoted run carries the staged doubled pair יפצחו וּפִצְח֥וּ - the unpointed written form beside the pointed read form - so the engagement names which forms it holds instead of resolving one away. The setumah cited at the verse close is inventoried under that exact type (single witness) and is the only mark at or inside this one-verse span, so symmetry is complete; petuchah is nowhere conflated with setumah in the row. Both edges are byte-distinct from the address: oshb:Isa.49.12 is third-person description opening with a presentative, and oshb:Isa.49.14 opens with a speech-report verb plus a named subject.

items.claim: Isolating the narrated complaint is defensible on voice, but the row omits the strongest byte device crossing its own back seam - the forget-root chain binding complaint to answer - and one stated seam ground is imprecise.
items.evidence: oshb:Isa.49.14 closes שְׁכֵחָֽנִי and the adjoining oshb:Isa.49.15 carries three tokens of the same root, opening הֲתִשְׁכַּ֤ח and closing אֶשְׁכָּחֵֽךְ - four occurrences across the two adjacent verses, all re-collated at byte tier. A consonantal sweep of that root returns 9 verses book-wide, and exactly TWO of them fall in this chapter: these two (skeleton tier, verse counts). A byte-true lexical chain straddling a row's own seam argues continuity against the cut and is owed a disclosure; the rejected alternative does consider the merge, but rests only on the voice contrast and never names the device, so the rival is disclosed while its actual evidence is not. Second, smaller: the stated ground that the next verse 'opens a new second-person address' is imprecise on the bytes - oshb:Isa.49.15 opens with a third-person rhetorical question about a woman and the son of her womb, and its only second-person element is the closing suffix in אֶשְׁכָּחֵֽךְ. What survives: the speech-attribution reading is byte-true (a wayyiqtol with a named subject at oshb:Isa.49.14), the deviation from the promise-oracle default is disclosed as the operative-category allowance requires, the setumah cited at oshb:Isa.49.13 is correctly typed, and no mark falls inside the span.

items.claim: The rationale's denial that any fresh imperative divides this span is byte-false: oshb:Isa.49.18 opens with a paired feminine-singular imperative, the same device class this cluster treats as a tier-1 driver five verses earlier.
items.evidence: oshb:Isa.49.18 opens שְׂאִֽי סָבִ֤יב עֵינַ֨יִךְ֙ וּרְאִ֔י at byte tier - two imperatives bracketing the addressed object, rendered as commands by both witnesses (web:Isa.49.18, 'Lift up your eyes all around, and see'). That is a verse-initial imperative-plus-address of exactly the form used as the tier-1 boundary driver for the one-verse doxology at oshb:Isa.49.13, so the stated universal - that no fresh imperative, vocative or messenger formula divides this run - is contradicted inside the row's own span. The row does single out this very verse in its rejected alternative, but only through the oath signature חַי אָ֣נִי נְאֻם יְהוָ֗ה, which it correctly holds as postpositive (this is one of the 23 oracle-signature verses, verse counts, and that signature is never an onset frame): the disclosed rival therefore rests on the one device at oshb:Isa.49.18 that is NOT a boundary candidate, while the device that is goes unnamed. What survives and should not be discarded in repair: the petuchah at oshb:Isa.49.21 is correctly typed and is the only mark in the span; the messenger frame at oshb:Isa.49.22 is byte-true as the next onset; and the second-person feminine address does run unbroken across oshb:Isa.49.15-Isa.49.21, with 2fs suffix tokens present in every verse of the run - real continuity evidence for the span as a whole. The defect is a false byte claim plus a misidentified rival at oshb:Isa.49.18, needing re-argument rather than deletion.

items.claim: The boundary survives on its messenger frame, but the declared driver - an addressee shift to the nations - is byte-false: the second-person feminine addressee is Zion, unbroken from the preceding span.
items.evidence: Byte-checked across oshb:Isa.49.22-Isa.49.23, every second-person form is feminine singular and continues the addressee of the preceding unit: בָנַ֨יִךְ֙ and וּבְנֹתַ֖יִךְ in the first verse; אֹֽמְנַ֗יִךְ וְשָׂרֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ מֵינִ֣יקֹתַ֔יִךְ, רַגְלַ֖יִךְ and the perfect opening וְיָדַ֨עַתְּ֙ כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה in the second. The nations are the goal and the third-person agents of the sentence - אֶל גּוֹיִם֙ with a plural verb of bringing - never the addressee. That feminine-singular address runs continuously from oshb:Isa.49.15 through oshb:Isa.49.23, with 2fs suffix tokens present in every verse of the run, so 'addressed to the nations rather than continuing' misstates what changes at the seam, and the declared addressee-shift signal, a dependent field of the driver, does not survive with it. What does hold at byte tier is the verse-initial divine messenger frame כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה (an inventoried divine frame, not a human-messenger one), a sufficient tier-1 onset on its own, so the cut itself is not in question - only its stated grounds and its declared signal. The petuchah at oshb:Isa.49.21 and the setumah at oshb:Isa.49.23 are correctly typed and never conflated. With device notes left empty, the continuing feminine address across the front seam is undisclosed as well, which is the same omission seen from the other direction.

items.claim: The row's own closing device is half of a byte-true recognition-formula pair bracketing across its front seam, and the verse-initial divine frame sitting inside the span is never argued from the bytes that would make it non-boundary.
items.evidence: The formula cited at this span's close, וְיָדְע֣וּ כָל בָּשָׂ֗ר כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.49.26, byte tier), shares its core with the formula closing the unit that ends at oshb:Isa.49.23, וְיָדַ֨עַתְּ֙ כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה (byte tier). A consonantal sweep of that shared core returns 4 verses book-wide, and two of them are precisely these adjacent unit-closes (skeleton tier, verse counts) - a bracketing device straddling the seam at oshb:Isa.49.23|Isa.49.24 that argues for one larger unit across it, disclosed on neither side of that seam. A second, weaker chain runs the length of the cluster undisclosed: the redeemer participle at oshb:Isa.49.7 and its suffixed form at oshb:Isa.49.26 are the only two sites of that root in chapters 49-50 (skeleton sweep: 21 verses book-wide, verse counts). Second defect: this span contains a verse-initial divine messenger frame of its own, כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.49.25, byte tier, an inventoried divine frame) - the identical device class used as the tier-1 boundary driver at oshb:Isa.49.7, oshb:Isa.49.8, oshb:Isa.49.22 and oshb:Isa.50.1. The row's rendering does carry the causal particle that is the real discriminator, but the row never argues from it, so one driver is applied at four seams and silently withheld at a fifth. What holds: the interrogative onset הֲיֻקַּ֥ח מִגִּבּ֖וֹר at oshb:Isa.49.24 is byte-true, and the setumah marks cited at both edges are correctly typed.

items.claim: The closing seam of this span is carried by a single-witness parashah mark plus a content observation, with no tier-1 byte signal named - although one sits in the next verse.
items.evidence: The opening is solid and re-collates at byte tier: כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה is verse-initial and divine at oshb:Isa.50.1 (an inventoried divine frame), and the interrogative chain is byte-present across the span - אֵ֣י זֶ֠ה and א֚וֹ מִ֣י in the first verse, מַדּ֨וּעַ and הֲקָצ֨וֹר in the second - so the form-based tagging and its disclosed deviation are byte-grounded, and the setumah at oshb:Isa.49.26 is correctly typed. At the back edge, however, the only signals offered are a content observation and the setumah at oshb:Isa.50.3; the parashah layer in the Prophets is weak single-witness corroboration and never a boundary driver, so this closing seam is left with no tier-1 ground, and no ref beyond the span appears in the evidence list to supply one. The bytes do supply it: oshb:Isa.50.4 opens אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה נָ֤תַן לִי֙ - a fronted divine title with a first-person recipient, turning from the divine first-person speech of this span to a first-person report about the speaker, and both witnesses render that turn the same way. Smaller residue: the pointed splice offered for oshb:Isa.50.2 is the whole verse while the paired rendering quoted from the English witness is only the mid-verse clause about the shortened hand, so quote and gloss are not cut to the same measure.
